subject: math
intro: This cluster worksheet covers displaying numerical data in dot plots, histograms, and box plots (6.SP.B.4), then summarizing data sets with measures of center and spread (6.SP.B.5). Items are grouped by standard and ramp from simple reading tasks to multi-step construction and interpretation.

items.prompt: A dot plot of the number of books read by students last month has dots above $0$ (3 dots), $1$ (5 dots), $2$ (4 dots), and $3$ (2 dots). How many students are represented in all?

steps: Each dot represents one student, so add up all the dots, not the number of distinct values.
Count the dots above each value: $3 + 5 + 4 + 2$.
There are $14$ students represented.

items.prompt: The number of pets owned by $10$ students is $0, 1, 1, 2, 0, 3, 1, 0, 2, 1$. If you build a dot plot, how many dots sit above each value $0$, $1$, $2$, and $3$?

steps: Tally how many times each value appears in the list.
Value $0$ appears at positions $1, 5, 8$, so $3$ times.
Value $1$ appears at positions $2, 3, 7, 10$, so $4$ times.
Value $2$ appears at positions $4, 9$, so $2$ times.
Value $3$ appears once at position $6$.
Check: $3 + 4 + 2 + 1 = 10$, which matches the $10$ students.

items.prompt: A histogram of test scores has the intervals $50\text{-}59$ (height $2$), $60\text{-}69$ (height $5$), $70\text{-}79$ (height $8$), $80\text{-}89$ (height $4$), and $90\text{-}99$ (height $1$). How many students scored at least $70$?

steps: "At least $70$" means the intervals $70\text{-}79$, $80\text{-}89$, and $90\text{-}99$.
Add their bar heights (frequencies): $8 + 4 + 1$.
So $13$ students scored at least $70$.

items.prompt: Using the same histogram from the previous item, where the interval $70\text{-}79$ has height $8$, exactly how many students scored a $73$? Explain.
items.answer: It is impossible to tell from the histogram.

steps: A histogram groups values into intervals; it only tells you how many values fall in each interval, not the individual values.
The interval $70\text{-}79$ has height $8$, meaning $8$ students scored somewhere from $70$ to $79$.
Those $8$ scores could be any mix of values in that range, so we cannot recover how many were exactly $73$.
A common mistake is to answer $8$, but that is the count for the whole interval, not the single value $73$.

items.prompt: Plant heights in centimeters are $4, 7, 9, 11, 12, 14, 18, 19, 21, 23$. Using equal-width intervals of width $5$ starting at $0$ ($0\text{-}4$, $5\text{-}9$, $10\text{-}14$, $15\text{-}19$, $20\text{-}24$), give the frequency (bar height) for each interval.

steps: Assign each value to the interval that contains it.
$0\text{-}4$: only $4$, so frequency $1$.
$5\text{-}9$: $7$ and $9$, so frequency $2$.
$15\text{-}19$: $18$ and $19$, so frequency $2$.
$20\text{-}24$: $21$ and $23$, so frequency $2$.
Check: $1 + 2 + 3 + 2 + 2 = 10$, matching the $10$ plant heights.

items.prompt: Order the data set $7, 3, 9, 5, 11, 8, 6, 10, 4$ and find the five-number summary: $\min$, $Q_1$, median, $Q_3$, and $\max$.

steps: There are $9$ values, so $\min = 3$ and $\max = 11$.
The median is the middle (5th) value: $7$.
The lower half (below the median) is $3, 4, 5, 6$; $Q_1$ is the average of its middle two: $\frac{4 + 5}{2} = \frac{9}{2}$.
The upper half (above the median) is $8, 9, 10, 11$; $Q_3$ is the average of its middle two: $\frac{9 + 10}{2} = \frac{19}{2}$.
Five-number summary: $\min = 3$, $Q_1 = \frac{9}{2}$, median $= 7$, $Q_3 = \frac{19}{2}$, $\max = 11$.

items.prompt: A box plot of quiz scores has $\min = 4$, $Q_1 = 7$, median $= 10$, $Q_3 = 13$, and $\max = 18$. What is the interquartile range (IQR)?

steps: The IQR measures the spread of the middle half of the data: $\text{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1$.
Substitute the values from the box plot: $\text{IQR} = 13 - 7$.
Note: $\max - \min = 18 - 4 = 14$ is the range, not the IQR, so do not report $14$.

items.prompt: The data set $12, 5, 9, 14, 7, 10, 6, 11, 8$ will be displayed in a box plot. Find the five-number summary and the IQR.

steps: With $9$ values, $\min = 5$ and $\max = 14$.
The median is the 5th value: $9$.

items.prompt: You want to display $200$ commute times so a reader can see how they group into ranges such as $0\text{-}9$ minutes, $10\text{-}19$ minutes, and so on, without listing every individual time. Which display (dot plot, histogram, or box plot) is most appropriate, and why?
items.answer: A histogram, because it groups a large data set into equal-width intervals and shows the frequency in each range.

steps: A dot plot needs one dot per value, so $200$ values would be cluttered and hard to read.
A box plot shows only the five-number summary, so it cannot show how the times group into many ranges.
A histogram bins the data into equal-width intervals and shows the frequency (bar height) for each range, which is exactly what is asked.
Therefore a histogram is the most appropriate display.

items.prompt: Two classes took the same test. Class A has a box plot with $Q_1 = 70$, median $= 78$, $Q_3 = 85$. Class B has a box plot with $Q_1 = 60$, median $= 78$, $Q_3 = 90$. The medians are equal. Which class has the greater spread in the middle half of its scores, and how do you know?
items.answer: Class B, because its IQR ($30$) is greater than Class A's IQR ($15$).

steps: The spread of the middle half of a data set is measured by the IQR $= Q_3 - Q_1$.
Class A: $\text{IQR} = 85 - 70 = 15$.
Class B: $\text{IQR} = 90 - 60 = 30$.
Even though the medians are equal at $78$, Class B has the larger IQR.
So Class B has the greater spread in the middle half of its scores.

items.prompt: A list gives the daily high temperature in degrees Fahrenheit for one week: $68, 71, 65, 70, 73, 69, 72$. State how many observations there are, what attribute is measured, and its units.
items.answer: $n = 7$ observations of daily high temperature, measured in degrees Fahrenheit.

steps: Count the values in the list: $68, 71, 65, 70, 73, 69, 72$ gives $7$ numbers, so $n = 7$ observations.
The attribute being measured is the daily high temperature.
The unit of measurement is degrees Fahrenheit.
So there are $7$ observations of daily high temperature in degrees Fahrenheit.

items.prompt: Find the mean and the median of the ordered data set $4, 7, 7, 9, 13$.

steps: Mean: add the values and divide by how many there are. $4 + 7 + 7 + 9 + 13 = 40$.
There are $5$ values, so the mean is $\frac{40}{5} = 8$.
Median: the data is already ordered, and with $5$ values the middle (3rd) value is the median.
The 3rd value is $7$, so the median is $7$.

items.prompt: For the data set $9, 3, 12, 6, 8, 5, 15, 18$, find the range and the interquartile range (IQR).

steps: Range $= \max - \min = 18 - 3 = 15$.
There are $8$ values, so the lower half is $3, 5, 6, 8$ and the upper half is $9, 12, 15, 18$.

items.prompt: Compute the mean absolute deviation (MAD) of the data set $2, 4, 6, 8$.

steps: First find the mean: $\frac{2 + 4 + 6 + 8}{4} = \frac{20}{4} = 5$.
Find the absolute deviation of each value from the mean: $|2 - 5| = 3$, $|4 - 5| = 1$, $|6 - 5| = 1$, $|8 - 5| = 3$.
Add the absolute deviations: $3 + 1 + 1 + 3 = 8$.
Divide by the number of values $n = 4$: $\text{MAD} = \frac{8}{4} = 2$.
Remember to keep the absolute values, otherwise the signed deviations would cancel to $0$.

items.prompt: House prices on a street are $\$210{,}000$, $\$220{,}000$, $\$230{,}000$, $\$240{,}000$, and $\$900{,}000$. Compute the mean and the median, then state which measure of center better summarizes a typical price and why.
items.answer: Mean $= \$360{,}000$, median $= \$230{,}000$. The median better summarizes a typical price because the single very high value ($\$900{,}000$) is an outlier that inflates the mean.

steps: Median: the data is already ordered, and with $5$ values the middle (3rd) value is $\$230{,}000$.
The value $\$900{,}000$ is an outlier, far above the cluster of prices near $\$210{,}000$ to $\$240{,}000$.
This outlier pulls the mean up to $\$360{,}000$, which is higher than every home except the outlier, so the mean is not typical.
The median $\$230{,}000$ sits among the bulk of the prices, so it better summarizes a typical price.
